title: Stride benchmark journal — 2026-11-04
body:
Context:
Small standalone sync (weekly perf/benchmarking) focused on an odd regression observed after the 0.9.3 kernel rollout and batching tweak (heuristic v2). This doc is a running journal of today's meeting, immediate test results, hypotheses, and concrete follow-ups. Informal notes — rough numbers come from quick smoke runs (dev cluster) and should not be used for SLA decisions until validated in dedicated shadow runs.

Attendees:
- Aisha (notes/owner)
- Liam (bench infra)
- Mateo (runtime kernel)
- Priya (observability)
- Eleni (platform / scheduling)

Agenda:
1) Reproduce regression pattern (p50 bump at low batch sizes, mixed-seq workloads)
2) Compare kv-cache + batching v2 vs baseline v1 across sequence mixes
3) Identify candidate root causes and immediate mitigations for canary
4) Assign follow-ups and schedule shadow runs

Summary of what we saw (brief):
- After kernel 0.9.3 + batching v2 rollout to canary (10% traffic), observed +12-18% p50 increase for mixed-seq (seq len 16/256 mix) at target QPS 1200 on dedicated-medium nodes. p95 and p99 mostly unchanged.
- Standalone synthetic runs on dev cluster reproduced p50 increase for small batch sizes (1-4) but not when batch auto-scaling forced max-batch=16.
- Spike correlation: tail of request arrival aligned with brief scheduler backpressure events (observability trace) which coincide with a timestamped kernel probe change (commit 5f8b2).

Quick smoke-run snapshot (dev cluster, model xlarge-ggml, 30s ramps, single node):
- baseline (kernel 0.9.2, batching v1): QPS 1350, p50 18ms, p95 62ms, mean batch size 2.1
- canary (kernel 0.9.3, batching v2): QPS 1320, p50 21ms, p95 64ms, mean batch size 1.9
- forced-large-batch (kernel 0.9.3, batching v2, max-batch=16): QPS 1290, p50 17ms, p95 63ms, mean batch size 7.3
Notes: baseline and forced-large-batch p50 similar; indicates batching v2 behavior at small batches might be introducing micro-latency.

Observations from traces/metrics:
- KV cache hit ratio unchanged (roughly 88%) across runs.
- CPU steal and host-level cgroup throttling spiked briefly during canary run; suspect scheduling interaction when batching v2 decides not to wait for coalescing.
- Thread-level sampling shows occasional contention on worker-queue mutex during microbursts (~200-400ms windows).
- GC activity: minimal (runtime is C++ python shim not the issue).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Batching v2 introduces a faster-emit path for small batches that avoids waiting for coalescing but pays in scheduling jitter when the scheduler preempts worker threads (leads to p50 bump).
2) Kernel probes in 0.9.3 changed the kernel-level timer granularity or introduced slight wake latency under cgroup pressure (commit 5f8b2).
3) Rare lock convoy on worker-queue interacting with the new batching path leading to micro-contention during arrival bursts.
4) Observability timing artifact (unlikely) — double-check clock sync across nodes.

Experiments to run (owner + ETA):
- E1: Reproduce dev smoke with real-time cpu affinity pinning (disable scheduler preemption) to test hypothesis #1 and #2. Owner: Liam. ETA: 2026-11-06.
- E2: Rollback batching v2 on canary only (keep kernel 0.9.3) to see if p50 returns to baseline. Owner: Aisha. ETA: 2026-11-05 (must coordinate with deploy window).
- E3: Instrument worker-queue mutex to log contention counts and add per-request timestamp to trace. Owner: Mateo. ETA: 2026-11-09.
- E4: Run a controlled cgroup stress test (burst CPU/IO) to see if kernel 0.9.3 behavior amplifies latency under throttling. Owner: Eleni. ETA: 2026-11-07.
- E5: Shadow run (dedicated-shadow with real traffic profile) with both baseline and canary configurations for 4 hours overnight, collect p10/p50/p90/p99 and batch size histograms. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2026-11-06 morning.

Immediate mitigations discussed:
- Hold canary at 10% and pause further rollout until E2/E5 results (agreed)
- Add a short coalescing delay in batching v2 as a quick toggle (feature-flagged) to test if small waits reduce p50. Quick patch target: Mateo/Liam pair. ETA: 2026-11-05 end of day.

Open questions / things to validate:
- Does forced large-batch penalize throughput under real customer mix? (We saw small QPS drop)
- Are there any cross-tenant noisy neighbor signals not captured by dev runs?
- Confirm kernel commit 5f8b2 exactly changes timer/wake behavior — ask infra kernel-wg for a micro-note. (Linked JIRA SRV-1482)

Notes-to-self / meeting artifacts:
- Attach trace IDs from canary: trace/2026-11-04-0812-aisha (put into JIRA SRV-1478)
- Add bench configs used to /bench/configs/stride/smoke-smallbatch-30s.yaml to the PR for reproducibility.

Decisions made:
- Pause rollout beyond 10% canary until follow-ups complete. (Aisha)
- Prioritize E2 (rollback batching v2 on canary) before kernel rollback — less blast radius.

Next sync:
- Quick async update in #bench-ops with smoke artifacts and E2 result (target 2026-11-05 COB)
- Full check-in Friday 2026-11-06 10:00 PT (15m) to review E1-E5 outputs and decide canary progression.

Action items (one-line):
- Aisha: coordinate E2 canary rollback + post result (2026-11-05)
- Liam: run cpu-affinity smoke and post p50/p95 histograms (2026-11-06)
- Mateo: add contention logging + small batching delay patch candidate (2026-11-09 for logging, 2026-11-05 for quick toggle)
- Priya: schedule 4h shadow, confirm data retention for histograms (2026-11-06 morning)
- Eleni: run cgroup stress test on cluster replicas (2026-11-07)

Unpolished notes / hypotheses repository:
- If hypothesis #1 is true, we should make batching v2 opt-in per-node and expose coalescing micros (0-5ms) as a runtime knob in console.
- If hypothesis #2 is true, coordinate with infra/kernel WG for a micro-patch and revert or shim the wake path for our nodes.

Comments / freeform: 
- Observed p95 stability is good; this suggests tail controls are intact but the user impact is subtle (p50 up -> more perceptible lag for light-weight calls). Important to protect PLG experience.
- Keep bench runs reproducible: always commit bench config + seed to PRs.

End of journal entry.

(If you read this and have a quick thought, drop it in the thread or mention Aisha)
